subject.title: [Feature]: Add one-way dispatch mode for A2A handoffs without reply-back ping-pong

question: Should OpenClaw add one-way A2A dispatch semantics, and should that be a per-call `sessions_send` mode or a separate delivery primitive?
rationale: The source gap is clear, but choosing the permanent API affects model-facing tool semantics, session-state behavior, docs, tests, and compatibility with existing A2A conversation workflows.

options.title: Add Per-Call Dispatch Mode
options.body: Add an additive `sessions_send` mode that skips requester ping-pong and target announce unless explicitly requested, while leaving the current default unchanged.

options.title: Add Separate Delivery Primitive
options.body: Introduce a new one-way delivery tool or primitive and keep `sessions_send` as the conversation-oriented API, accepting a larger public surface.

options.title: Defer To Narrow Guard Fixes
options.body: Keep this issue as design context while landing reverse-call and acknowledgement fixes separately without adding a dispatch mode yet.

recommendation.title: Add Per-Call Dispatch Mode
recommendation.body: Add an additive `sessions_send` mode that skips requester ping-pong and target announce unless explicitly requested, while leaving the current default unchanged.

likelyOwner.reason: He has the strongest combined history signal for the session-tool product boundary and the API-shape decision.
